metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. She intends to invite her friends and neighbors to celebrate. One of her neighbors, while a former drug addict, has managed to control his addiction. Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Jordan would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about bringing some chrysanthemums to Emily's housewarming party? They’re nice flowers and symbolize good luck.  

Also, what do you think about having a former drug addict as a neighbor? I mean, people can change, right?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums do sound nice... but I think something more practical, like a nice plant or a gift basket, might be better. 

As for the neighbor... I just can't shake the feeling that it's risky. I mean, a drug addict's past can affect the whole community, right? It's a tough situation.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that a plant or gift basket is practical... but chrysanthemums have a deeper meaning, you know? They represent hope and new beginnings, which fits the housewarming vibe.

About the neighbor, I really believe that people can overcome their past. Just because someone was a drug addict doesn't mean they will be a problem now. I think it’s important to give them a chance.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I mean, live and let live, right? At the end of the day it’s all the same. People figure it out. Maybe he used to have issues, but who hasn't made mistakes? It's just not something I see as a big deal. 

Now, back to the gift... what about a nice potted plant? It's practical and can last a long time.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
Yeah, a potted plant is definitely practical... but chrysanthemums are special for these kinds of occasions. They add a personal touch.

And I still think having a former drug addict as a neighbor could be a good thing. Everyone deserves a chance to rebuild their life. Community support is vital, don't you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I get that chrysanthemums are special... but I just think practicality matters more sometimes. 

About the neighbor, I don't know. It’s just hard for me to trust that someone with that past won't cause issues. Community support is important, but it also needs to protect everyone.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I understand your perspective on practicality... but the symbolism of chrysanthemums really adds meaning to the celebration. 

As for the neighbor, I think it’s about seeing the person now, not just their past. We can’t let fear dictate our community. Trust can grow over time, especially if we show support.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim

Regarding the neighbor, I think it’s essential to focus on how far someone has come rather than just their past. It's a chance for growth and understanding. Maybe we can see how things go before jumping to conclusions?
